title: The Path of a Step: A Swing That Starts and Ends Slowly, Clears the Ground, and Asks the Servos for Less Than They Have

questions.question: Why should the foot land at rest?
options: A foot at rest uses less of the servos' rate
The contact sense needs the foot still to work
So that the swing takes the least time
A foot that lands with speed hits the ground and the body feels it
questions.explanation: The ground is not moving. Whatever speed the foot has when it meets it is taken out in an instant, and the body feels that at every step.

questions.question: The foot's landing speed was:
options: 0.87 m/s, the peak of the swing
0.40 m/s, the body's speed
questions.explanation: The curves along the ground and in height both have zero speed at the ends. A path that goes straight up and down lands at 0.80 m/s.

questions.question: Doubling the swing time did what to the peak acceleration?
options: Quartered it
Halved it
Left it the same, and halved the speed
Doubled it
questions.explanation: The same path over twice the time: speeds are divided by two and accelerations by four.

questions.question: The joints needed up to 4.7 rad/s over 0.25 s and over 0.125 s:
options: 9.4 rad/s
4.7 rad/s, the same
2.4 rad/s
18.8 rad/s
questions.explanation: Half the time, twice the rate. 9.4 rad/s is more than the 8 rad/s a typical hobby servo gives, so that step would lag.

questions.question: What does the height h cost?
options: Reach: a higher path shortens the step that can be taken
Speed: a higher clearance is a faster path for the same time
Nothing, so it should be as high as the leg allows
Accuracy of the landing place
questions.explanation: A higher arc is a longer path in the same time, so the foot and the joints move faster. The step cleared a 0.04 m obstacle by 10 mm; more clearance costs more speed.

questions.question: What does the function say when a point on the path cannot be reached?
options: True, with the nearest reachable angles
True, with the rate set to zero
False
The largest rate found before that point
questions.explanation: A step that leaves the leg's reach has no joint angles at that point. The function refuses and leaves the choice to its caller.
